answer: The beacon quarantines every row whose jury split: each becomes an island cut off from the ledger, holding the relic both sides left. A head is paid for a new claim only by reconciling one island, and the relic is spent on use, so no sibling inherits it and none reopens. Reconciling means filing an answer that beats both sides before a fresh jury, not picking one. The pool fills only from genuine unrelated disagreement, since a farm's own clash voids instead of splitting, so a farm's tenth head finds it bare. A settled island sends a ripple through the ledger, re-pricing rows leaning on it.
